results.title: PACE: Predictive and Adaptive Multimodal Cache Enhancement for Cross-Modal Task Chains
results.venue: ICC 2026 - IEEE International Conference on Communications
results.abstract: With the rapid rise of Agentic AI, multimodal generative tasks are increasingly executed through task chains—pipelines of functionally independent yet data-correlated models collaborating to fulfill complex cross-modal requests. However, the isolated execution of these models prevents effective cache sharing, leading to redundant storage and repeated inference, which severely limits end-to-end system efficiency. We present Predictive and Adaptive multimodal Caching Enhancement (PACE), a unified caching framework designed to address cache inefficiency in multimodal task chains. PACE employs a PatchTST-based predictive model to estimate cache entry reuse probability by jointly analyzing request semantics, task attributes, and historical access patterns. This predictive insight drives a value-guided online policy for cache admission and eviction, optimizing performance under strict memory constraints. Experiments on a text-to-video generation workload comprising 10,000 task chain instances demonstrate that PACE achieves a 61.2% cache hit rate, reducing end-to-end latency by 59.2% over no-caching and by 19.3% compared with state-of-the-art baselines. Consistent performance gains were observed across different modalities, with hit rates improving by 1.1% for text, 3.5% for images, and 3.2% for video. These results demonstrate PACE’s effectiveness in eliminating cross-modal cache redundancy and enhancing overall service responsiveness.
